caption: What if you tried to count every star in the sky? From a big city, you might see only the brightest dozen. Go somewhere truly dark on a moonless night and about 2,000 stars appear at once. India's first dark sky reserve, around Hanle in Ladakh, was declared in 2022 to protect skies like that. Add up both halves of the planet's sky and your eyes top out at roughly 9,000 to 10,000 stars. But our Milky Way holds an estimated 100 to 400 billion. Counting just 100 billion, one per second without a break, would take over 3,000 years. And the whole Universe may hold 10^22 to 10^24 stars, likely more than all the sand grains on Earth's beaches. Bonus: the Geminid meteor shower peaks on 13-14 December, with a thin crescent Moon, though shooting stars are dust, not stars. Plot twist: you can count one star in broad daylight. It's the Sun. How many stars can YOU see from your roof tonight? 👇
